office_does: The prosecuting attorney charges and tries criminal cases for the state in Kitsap County, defends lawsuits against the county, and is legal adviser to county government and school districts.
race_blurb: Two Democrats. Incumbent Chad M. Enright, prosecutor since 2019, runs on his diversion programs, staffing record and broad institutional endorsements. Public defender and former deputy prosecutor Joe Lombardi says the office is mismanaged and pledges to refuse corporate PAC money and keep ICE out of county cases.

candidates.summary: Kitsap County Prosecutor since 2019 and in the office since 2008; runs on diversion and treatment-court programs, full staffing, balanced budgets and endorsements from the county party, the deputy prosecutors' guild and the attorney general.
highlights: Created Kitsap's first pre-arrest diversion program and the North Kitsap Recovery Resource Center diversion [S3][S6]
Says violent crime, sex offenses and crimes against vulnerable people remain the priority [S5]
Plans race-blind charging and a real-time public case-data website [S1]
Reports all prosecutor positions filled and no case backlog [S1][S3]
Endorsed by Kitsap County Democrats, the DPA Guild, AG Nick Brown and former sheriffs Gese and Simpson [S4][S5]

experience.basis: Eight-year incumbent with 18 years in the office; makes experience and management record the central contrast.

safety.basis: Record of building pre-arrest diversion, recovery-center diversion and therapeutic courts, while keeping violent and sex crimes as the stated priority.

reform.basis: Campaigns on endorsements from every local Democratic elected official, the county party and allied organizations.

candidates.summary: Kitsap County public defender and former Kitsap deputy prosecutor and assistant attorney general who says the prosecutor's office is mismanaged and runs on changing its culture.
highlights: Says a 'toxic management culture' has driven experienced prosecutors out and led to erratic charging [S4]
Would personally prosecute the most serious violent cases and expand diversion for low-level offenders [S1][S2]
Pledges to keep ICE out of county cases and prosecute unlawful federal enforcement actions [S1][S2]
Refuses contributions from corporate PACs and special interests [S2]
Endorsed by the Kitsap County Central Labor Council [S3]

experience.basis: Challenger with no elected or supervisory experience who runs on changing the office ('I am not a politician'), while citing a decade of legal practice.

reform.basis: Refuses contributions from corporate PACs and special interests.

safety.basis: Would expand diversion and mental-health services for low-level offenders while prioritizing violent crime and enforcing probation.
